simple.meaning: בִּלְדַּד (Bildad) is a Hebrew word meaning “Bildad , one of Job's friends.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: בִּלְדַּד (H1085) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 2:11, with occurrences in Job.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בִּלְדַּד (H1085) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in בִּלְדַּד (H1085) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: בִּלְדַּד (Bildad) / H1085 is traced through Job 2:11, Job 8:1, Job 18:1, Job 25:1 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

evidence: Lexicon or morphology identifies this as a proper name

firstOccurrence.englishText: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.

majorEvents.label: Divine acceptance
majorEvents.evidenceText: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did what Yahweh commanded them, and Yahweh accepted Job.

definitions.full: H1085.
